correctness.rationale: For the shortest full-alphabet prefix ending at r, its last letter has no earlier occurrence. Patterns beginning with that letter force their remaining positions into the suffix starting at r+g+1; conversely every first letter can be chosen at or before r and joined to a suffix embedding. Iteration, with no spacer after the kth required arch, proves the unique decomposition, including words with more than k arches. It makes spacer deletion and insertion mutually inverse with q^(g(k-1)) choices. Enumerating successive first arrivals gives arch series A_q. Multiplication gives the cumulative series; subtracting consecutive cumulative series yields the exact-index law, including the empty word. The coefficient one above minimum is obtained by extending exactly one arch or the arbitrary tail by one letter. On an i.i.d. uniform source, stopping at each arch and skipping a deterministic g letters leaves fresh i.i.d. input. Thus completion times are sums of independent coupon-collector lengths plus g(k-1), and inverse strong law gives the stated limit. The limit is for the length guaranteed for all patterns, not the achievable length of a single favored pattern.
residual_risks: The three-length literal checks corroborate but do not prove the formulas. The infinite calculation requires uniform i.i.d. source letters and no upper gap bound.

evidence: Set B=(qz)^g. An incomplete alphabet word has generating function I_q=(1-F_q)/(1-qz); the indexed tail factor is then T=(1-F_q B)/(1-qz). Substituting gives the exact bivariate formula, and summing over indices m>=k yields F_q^k B^(k-1)/(1-qz).

The indexed unique decomposition gives the same deletion/insertion of k-1 spacers after the first k arches. Expanding its cumulative series gives the one-extra-position count. On independent input the identical decomposition gives independent coupon-collector blocks, so adding a fixed spacer to each block yields the stated renewal rate by the ordinary strong law.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the ordinary arch theorem nor the edit-radius result alone states the positive-gap structure, but the matching indexed theorem does; the remaining refinements are mechanical consequences and do not supply a distinct claim.
